verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'not her choice of subject' — the essay names only the style and never contrasts it with subject matter
verdicts.trueWording: Something about the style does not lend itself to shorter tales
verdicts.note: Wayback raw id_ capture fetched; quote verbatim in the opening paragraph, preceded by 'Robin Hobb seems unable to write anything that is less than a novella in length', so the novella limb holds. But the exclusive contrast is added by the claim: Hobb never sets style against subject, and a few lines later she attributes short-story difficulty to inspiration ('Either I get a wonderful idea for a short story, and I write it, or I don't'), which cuts against 'not her choice of subject'. Drop the contrast and the claim verifies.
